name: Carter Takes Nasal Medication
description: Carter tilts his head back and dispenses drops into his nose.
related_events: Carter administers nasal drops to himself

name: Carter Steadies Himself in the Corridor
description: Carter walks down the corridor, moving forward while bracing himself as he goes.
related_events: Carter moves along the corridor and steadies himself

name: Train Enters Tunnel and Vanishes into Darkness
description: The express train speeds forward and enters a tunnel, instantly plunging into complete darkness as the surrounding walls close in and block out all light.

name: Jack Carter Reads a Novel on a Crowded Train
description: Jack Carter sits in a corner of a crowded train compartment, holding a copy of Raymond Chandler's Farewell My Lovely. He turns the pages steadily, his eyes moving across the text as the train rumbles forward. Around him, the compartment remains full, passengers shifting in their seats, but he stays focused on the book.
related_events: Jack Carter reads Farewell My Lovely on a crowded train

name: Carter Shaves by the Coffin
description: Carter moves around the coffin, guiding his electric razor over his face. The razor is plugged into a lamp mounted above his dead brother’s coffin, its cord stretched taut as he shifts position. He continues his routine, the hum of the razor filling the quiet room.
related_events: Carter shaves near his dead brother's coffin

name: Train Emerges from Tunnel into Evening Light
description: The train bursts out of a dark tunnel, emerging into the glow of evening light that spills across the tracks. The landscape opens around it, bathed in the dim, slanting rays of the setting sun, as the train races forward along the rails.

name: The Horses Burst from the Starting Gates

related_events: Albert Swift sees Carter and reacts in shock

name: Carter Follows the Cadillac onto a Minor Road

related_events: Cadillac turns onto a minor road
Carter begins following a Cadillac on a country road

Ray and Marty rush into the house in pursuit

related_events: Albert steps on a hot dog causing ketchup to ooze out

description: The hearse stands parked outside a row of terraced houses. The young undertaker, standing nearby, turns his head to watch as Doreen Carter walks up the street. She is sixteen, with long, lank hair and clothes that are ill-fitting and cheap, though styled to make her look older. Without hesitation, she walks up to Frank's house and goes inside. The undertaker remains by the hearse, his eyes fixed on the door she entered.

Young girl approaches and enters Frank's house

Carter retrieves his coat and briefcase from the overhead rack

name: Carter Follows Cadillac to The Heights

Carter parks his vehicle

description: The funeral cortege turned into the crematorium driveway. As it approached, the occupants saw a Land Rover parked outside. Inside were two men who had been seen near Frank's house. The cortege passed the vehicle as another long funeral procession began moving out, the two groups passing in opposite directions.

Cortege passes Land Rover with two suspicious men

The drinks compartment is open, and the men pour themselves glasses of champagne, passing the bottle between them. description: The room is dark. A light snaps on, illuminating the face of Frank Carter lying in a coffin, his eyes closed, skin pale and still. Carter enters, approaches the coffin, and gently touches his brother's crossed hands. He folds the shroud over the man's face, then turns, walks to the door, reaches for the switch, and turns off the light. He closes the door behind him, leaving the room in darkness.

Carter touches his brother's hands and covers his face with shroud
Carter exits the room and turns off the light

description: Edna Garfoot climbs the stairs, her figure steady and deliberate. Carter follows behind, carrying his baggage, his eyes briefly lingering on her. As they ascend, he says he won’t be using the room tonight. Edna stops, turns to face him, and asks if the friend he’s staying with has a husband due back tomorrow. Carter smiles and tells her it’s not like that. Edna resumes climbing, remarking that it never is.

Carter informs Edna he will not use the room tonight

Heads turn toward her. Carter leans toward Doreen and whispers, 'Is that Margaret?' Doreen nods in response. The vicar continues speaking as the coffin disappears beneath the catafalque.

As the service continues, the coffin begins to descend, slowly sinking out of sight. At that moment, a woman enters the chapel. The sound of her high heels clunks sharply against the floor, breaking the silence. Everyone turns to look. Carter leans toward Doreen and whispers, 'Is that Margaret?' Doreen nods. The coffin disappears from view.

description: The rain stops, and spectators lower their umbrellas. Horses surge forward in a thundering sprint toward the finishing post. Jockeys lean low and whip their mounts as turf flies in all directions. The crowd roars with excitement.

related_events: Bookies and punters lower their umbrellas after the rain stops

Two men survey the scene from the Land Rover
Two men drive away after surveying the scene

name: The Undertaker Waits in the Hearse

name: Edna and Carter Secure the Room
description: The door opens and the light goes on. It's a big room overlooking the road, furnished cheaply but comfortably. Edna and Carter enter, talking. Edna asks if Carter is a traveler. He smiles and says he definitely is. She looks around the room and asks if it will do. Carter looks around and says it's very nice. He takes his wallet out and offers to pay for that night as well. Edna tells him not to be bloody silly, saying he's the first since Monday, but Carter gives her the money anyway. She thanks him. Carter feels the mattress and says he'll bet it's seen some action. He smiles at her and she looks back, expressionless. Edna tells him she'll give him the key when he comes down, then closes the door.
related_events: Edna and Carter enter the room and begin talking
Carter offers to pay Edna for the night

name: Test the Mattress and Exchange a Look

Edna gives Carter the key before leaving

name: Carter Sees Men in Land Rover
description: Carter hears a vehicle stop outside. He moves to the window and gently pulls back the old net curtain. Two men in a Land Rover are looking up at his window. When they see him, they quickly drive away.
related_events: Carter observes two men in a Land Rover looking up at his window

As he holds them, his expression changes, briefly lost in thought. He places the shotgun on the unmade bed, then turns and leaves the room, stepping out onto the landing.

Carter finds a box of cartridges on the wardrobe
Carter experiences a flood of memories about growing up with Jack and Frank

Carter picks up a dead branch, runs toward the man, and strikes him on the head. The man collapses unconscious into the water. Carter leaves the scene and moves toward the house.

description: Carter moves through the trees toward a Victorian house surrounded by woodland. He steps out from the tree line and sprints across the open ground toward the side door. On the lawn, two men, Marty and Ray, are playing with an Alsatian. One of them sees Carter and shouts after him.

name: Two Men Transport a Coffin
description: Two men in long grey coats stand in silence in the corridor. The coffin comes into view. Without speaking, they lift it and place it onto a trolley with practiced ease. One of the men begins whistling as they push the trolley down the wide corridor toward the furnace.

name: Carter Watches the Hearse with Eddie and Keith
description: Carter sits in the limousine, looking through the windscreen at his brother's coffin as it moves ahead in the hearse. The procession winds slowly through the city streets. In the front seats, Eddie and Keith talk about Carter's brother. Keith says he couldn't believe it when he heard the news, that he was surprised when the brother didn't show up for work, since he was always on time. He mentions working with him at the Half Moon. Eddie chimes in, saying it's strange—knowing a man for six years, thinking he's as calm as gentle Jesus, and then he does something like this. He shakes his head. Carter answers quietly, 'Yeah. A bloody funny thing.'
related_events: Carter observes his brother's coffin being transported through the city
Eddie reflects on the unexpected nature of Carter's brother's actions
Carter quietly agrees with Eddie's reflection on his brother's actions

name: Keith Reveals He Worked with Carter's Brother

Keith says he couldn't believe it when he heard the news, explaining he was surprised when Carter's brother didn't show up for work—he was always on time. Carter turns his attention to Keith and asks if they worked together. Keith replies that they did, at the Half Moon.

description: The undertakers maneuver the coffin down a narrow staircase and into the street. Outside, Carter and Doreen stand with two other men, waiting. Eddie Appleyard, a middle-aged man in a shabby tweed suit, cap, and black tie, speaks with them. He says they weren’t sure where the funeral was taking place. Carter thanks him for coming. Eddie replies that Frank was a good bloke. Keith Lacey, a young barman who worked with Frank, agrees, saying he was that. Eddie adds that Frank was one of the best.

Carter and Doreen wait outside with two men

Eddie Appleyard, wearing a shabby tweed suit, a cap, and a black tie, approached with Keith Lacey. Carter greeted them, saying it was nice of them to come. Eddie replied that they hadn't been sure where the funeral was taking place. Keith nodded, and Eddie added that Frank was a good bloke. Keith agreed, saying he was that, and Eddie said he was one of the best.

Carter replies sarcastically, commenting on Cyril's stance. Eric adds that Sid and Gerald will also be unhappy when they find out Carter has been interfering. description: During the funeral service for Doreen's father, Carter asks her how school is going. Doreen tells him she left school last year and now works at Woolworths. Carter says that must be interesting, and they look at each other in silence. He then asks if she plans to live with Margaret. Doreen hesitates, shakes her head, and searches in her bag for a cigarette. Carter suggests she come with him and his fiancée to South America, saying she wouldn't mind and adding that her father would have wanted it. An undertaker nearby calls to a colleague to get Hughbert and then tells Carter they are ready.

description: Carter stands in a scrapyard beside the River Tyne, looking over a battered Hillman. He runs his hand over the dented metal, studying it closely. Carter asks what happened to the car. Billy replies that it ended up in the river. Carter inquires whether the steering was faulty, but Billy shakes his head. He then asks about the brakes, and Billy insists they were fine. Carter presses for an explanation, and Billy tells him the driver—Carter’s brother—was drunk, very drunk, and that he drove the car into the river himself.

description: The door opens slowly, and Doreen stands in the doorway, staring at her father's coffin. Carter sees her and steps forward. 'Doreen?' he says. She doesn't respond, her gaze fixed. 'All right, are you?' he asks. She remains silent. 'Been staying with a friend?' Carter says. Doreen nods. The undertaker coughs nearby and tightens another screw into the coffin lid. 'Sorry about your father,' Carter says. After a pause, Doreen answers, 'Yeah.' 'Tell me, Doreen, did the police say anything?' She looks dazed. 'They said he was drunk.'

description: A telephone rings in the bar. The second barman answers and asks if there is a Mr. Carter present. Carter confirms it and walks to the far end of the bar to pick up the receiver. He says, 'Hello?' and after a pause, asks, 'Margaret?' He lights a cigarette and questions why she isn't there, then asks what time it is. He inquires if Doreen is at the house and, after another pause, asks who is with him then. He presses for when he can see her and asks if she will be there the next day. As he begins to say, 'Now listen, Margaret...', the line goes dead. Carter hangs up the telephone.

name: Carter Confronts Eric at the Racetrack
description: Carter stands near the saddling ring at the racetrack, scanning the crowd. His gaze settles on Eric Paice, who is dressed in a grey chauffeur's uniform, wearing a cap, dark glasses, and gloves. Eric stands close to three well-dressed men holding binoculars and shooting sticks as horses are led around the enclosure. Carter moves in from behind and speaks. 'Grey suits you, Eric.' Eric turns quickly, startled. 'Good God! Jack Carter.' Carter smiles. 'Eric. Eric Paice.' Eric asks what he is doing there. Carter replies that it's his hometown. Eric says he didn't know. Carter takes out a pack of cigarettes, offers one, and lights it for him. Eric thanks him. Carter asks who he is working for now. Eric says he's straight and respectable. Carter jokes about Martini, then presses again. He names Brumby and Kinnear, but Eric shakes his head at each. 'What's it to you anyway?' Eric asks. Carter says he's always cared about Eric's welfare and admits he's nosy. Eric warns that nosiness isn't always healthy. A track announcement interrupts. Carter comments that Eric seems to be doing well, making good. Eric says he's just making a living. Carter asks about prospects, a pension, then reaches up and removes Eric's sunglasses. He looks into his eyes. 'I'd almost forgotten what your eyes looked like. They're still the same. Piss holes in the snow.' Eric stares back. 'Still got a sense of humour?' Carter says he has. He starts to walk toward the saddling ring and turns. 'Do you know a man called Albert Swift, Eric?' Eric says he doesn't. Carter looks across the track. 'Don't miss the start on my account.'

Carter jokes about the uniform, suggesting he’s advertising Martini, then removes Eric’s sunglasses to look at his eyes, calling them 'piss holes in the snow.' Eric responds dryly that Carter still has a sense of humor. Carter moves toward the saddling ring and asks if Eric knows a man named Albert Swift. Eric says he doesn’t. Carter tells him not to miss the start of the race.

Carter looks out across the racetrack, then tells Eric not to miss the start of the race. Without another word, he moves away, leaving Eric behind.

name: A Toast and a Doubt at the Bar
description: Eddie raises his glass to absent friends and drinks, then quietly wonders if Frank might have killed himself on purpose. Keith laughs at the idea, saying Frank wasn't the type and had no worries, especially since they worked together every day. Carter challenges him, asking why Frank had started drinking whisky, a habit no one seems to know about. Doreen begins to cry. Eddie finishes his drink and calls Frank a good bloke. Doreen suddenly shouts that none of them knew Frank, throws her drink in Eddie's face, and runs out, sobbing. Keith starts to follow, but Carter stops him, telling him to let her go. Carter offers Eddie another drink, but Eddie declines, saying he should get to work. Carter presses money into Eddie's pocket for his suit, and Eddie leaves, saying Frank was a good man. Carter asks Keith if he works there, then tells him to pass on word if anyone asks for him. He says he's staying at the Las Vegas, behind the dance hall. Carter asks if Keith knows Albert Swift. Keith says he does, and that he’s likely at the races. Carter takes out a small phial of pills and says he went to school with Albert, that he was the leader of their gang.

name: Doreen Reveals She Is Frank's Daughter and Storms Out
description: Doreen, sitting with Carter, Keith, and Eddie at the pub, grows increasingly distressed as the men talk about Frank. When Eddie calls Frank a 'bloody good bloke' and says he was one of the best, Doreen suddenly blurts out, 'How would you know?' She stands up, grabs her glass, and throws the contents in Eddie's face, shouting, 'None of you knew. I knew. He was me dad.' Then she runs out of the pub, crying. Keith starts to follow, but Carter stops him by putting out a hand. 'Let her go. She'll be OK,' Carter says.

Carter then turned to Eddie and offered him another drink. Eddie declined, saying he needed to get to work. He stood up, cap in hand. Carter pulled out a wad of money, peeled off a note, and insisted Eddie take it to clean his suit. Eddie wiped his face with a handkerchief, thanked Carter, and left the pub.

name: Carter Confronts Margaret in the Cloisters
description: Carter emerges from the chapel and sees Margaret walking quickly down the cloisters, past the memorial tablets and urns. He calls out to her. Margaret stops, turns, and waits as Carter approaches. They stand facing each other in silence for a moment before speaking.

name: Margaret Denies Knowing Doreen
description: Carter tells Margaret he wants to talk about Doreen. Margaret stops walking and looks back at the girl, who is standing at the end of the cloisters, watching them. 'She's nothing to do with me,' Margaret says firmly. Carter frowns, reminding her that she's been with Frank since Doreen's mother left and that she's closer to the girl than anyone. Margaret shakes her head, insisting it's not like that, and says she has a husband. She starts walking again, faster. Carter grabs her arm to stop her. 'Who killed Frank, Margaret?' he asks. She looks nervous, says she doesn't know anything about it, and pulls away. She hurries off, saying she has to go. Carter calls after her, asking to talk again. After a pause, she agrees to meet him the next morning at twelve o'clock on the Iron Bridge. She walks away quickly, her high heels clicking on the stone. Carter and Doreen both watch her leave.

Margaret shakes her head, her voice nervous as she says she doesn’t know anything about it. She pulls away and starts walking quickly again. Carter follows, telling her he wants to talk later. name: Carter Arrives and Orders a Drink
description: Carter pushes open the pub door and moves through the packed, noisy room, making his way to the bar. The trio on stage plays a loud, driving tune as the busty pub singer performs under the dim lights. Keith, the bartender, sees him and calls out, 'What you having, Jack?' 'Large Scotch,' Carter replies, his eyes briefly scanning the room, settling on the singer. The crowd cheers and whistles as she sways on stage. Keith returns with the drink, sets it down, and quietly asks if Carter’s heard of a man called Thorpe. Carter watches the singer, sipping his Scotch as the music continues to play.

name: Keith Asks About Thorpe
description: Carter enters the pub and pushes through the crowded room to the bar, where Keith serves him a large Scotch. On stage, a big, busty singer performs with a trio behind her, the music loud and driving. As Carter watches her, Keith leans in and asks if he’s heard of a man called Thorpe. Carter replies that he knows him—'Old Thorpey'—and hasn’t seen him in a while. Keith picks up Carter’s money, heads to the till, then returns, saying Thorpe had heard Carter was in town and wanted to know where he was staying, mentioned wanting to look him up for old times’ sake. Carter says that’s nice and asks what Keith told him. Keith says he told him nothing. Carter calls him a good lad, finishes his drink, and says he’ll see Keith later. When Keith asks where he’s off to, Carter smiles and says, 'Las Vegas.' He starts toward the door. The singer has left the stage and is moving between tables, pausing to kiss a man at one of them. The crowd cheers. The woman sitting with the man suddenly snaps, grabs his beer, and throws it in the singer’s face, then yanks her hair and pulls her to the ground. The two women roll on the floor, punching and scratching as Carter stops to watch.

Carter looks hurt and pauses. He asks where she will live instead. She tells him she will stay at her friend's house on Wilton Estate. 'Bollock naked with his socks still on?' he says, removing his cigar. Sid muses that people do that up North. Gerald wonders if it's for protection, then laughs. Jack Carter, holding a drink, turns away to the cocktail cabinet as the next slide appears. Sid comments on the physical flexibility required in another image—'Must be a bloody contortionist.' Gerald reacts with mock disgust to a pair of suede boots, then shifts focus to Jack, warning him against going North. He warns that those connections could be damaged if Jack goes there. He mentions that hard men operate in that region and that they won’t take kindly to an outsider interfering. 'I'd hate you to screw 'em up,' Gerald says. Jack replies, 'Too bad.' Gerald leans forward. 'I smell trouble, boy.' Sid interjects, 'The law was satisfied.' Jack stands firm.
